description.narrative: Civil Rights Defenders föreslår att arbeta genom en koncentrerad insats med både etablerade och nya och framtida mänskliga rättighetsorganisationer och HRD i Etiopien -- för att stärka kapaciteten för denna avgörande civilsamhällsgrupp under den fortsatta demokratiska övergången, före, under och bortom de planerade nationella valen.

Civil Rights Defenders proposes to work through a concentrated effort with both established and new and up-­-coming human rights organizations and HRDs in Ethiopia -­- to strengthen the capacity of this crucial civil society group throughout the continued democratic transition, before, during and beyond the planned national elections.

The main objective of this intervention has been to revitalize and strengthen human rights organizations and human rights defenders in Ethiopia through participatorydriven capacity collaboration and strengthening. To achieve this, the following mutually reinforcing pillars has been serving as sub-objectives: 1) Support in building institutional capacity 2) Strengthening security capacity 3) Increasing knowledge of and ability to advocate for human rights 4) Expanding human rights networking.
The implementation of these sub-objectives has been structured according to the following main components and expected results: Component 1: Financial and administrative capacity strengthening Expected results: 1. Improved understanding of financial administrative system of civil society organizations 2. Increased overall capacity of organizations with efficient and sustainable financial and administrative systems
Component 2: Security Capacity Strengthening Expected results: 1. Strengthened capacity and improved knowledge of existing and emerging HRDs on physical, psychosocial, and digital security 2. Increased ability of human rights defenders to systematically conduct human rights monitoring and advocacy
Component 3: Strengthening human rights networking, advocacy, and communications Expected results: 1. Increased capacity of human rights defenders to conduct human rights advocacy 2. Improved access to information providing better advocacy programs

Component 1: Financial and administrative capacity strengthening Results achieved: • 14 Implementing Partners (IPs) have gradually built a better understanding of their financial and organisational capacity, supported by the organisational capacity assessments (OCA) which were conducted and from which they´ve received individual organisational capacity reports. They´ve built knowledge through this assessment process where the consultants shared relevant insights in different aspects of their organisational capacity. Four of the partners have also produced their own capacity development action plan. Further, a Capacity Development Guideline with short term and long term action plans has been developed, which can be used as a key reference material for IPs to track their capacity progress.
• Building on the findings of the OCA and partners own priorities, the overall financial and administrative capacity of the partners have been improved by subsequent interventions. Some of them abled to purchase and start using accounting systems which enhance their financial efficiency. IPs were, through grants and coaching, able to maintain staff, developed strategic plans and/or different manuals that are necessary to standardize and streamline their internal financial and administrative processes. CRD supported development of internal capacity-oriented manuals/guidelines that can be adapted easily by small and medium sized CSOs; Human Resource Manual, Financial Management Manual, Procurement Manuel and Capacity Development Guideline. These manuals will have a long-term use for existing and future capacity support efforts.
•The project has enabled 18 young women HRDs, three of them with disabilities, to get internship opportunities to work in human rights organisations. The seven hosting IPs in turn gained a lot from the new energy and insights of the internship participants. This mutually beneficial arrangement further resulted in majority of the participants to be hired in the human rights sector including the national Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC).
• CRD´s organisational capacity support coaching and grants enhanced the capacity of 15 partners to execute their projects more effectively. In addition to strengthening financial and admin capabilities, partners have been enabled to implement their project more efficiently. For some, CRD´s support was key to increase the quality of their monitoring and documentation of violations; two partners provided training for 20 social media influencers from Addis Ababa and Gambella on human rights, with specific focus on womens rights and rights of persons with disability for advocacy purposes.
Component 2: Security Capacity Strengthening Results Achieved • 10 IPs and Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) working in the organizations have an improved knowledge and understanding of digital security. They have improved their awareness on the threats on digital devices and online. The participants have learned tools necessary to protect their security and privacy.
• 15 Women Human Rights Defenders (WHRDs) have increased their digital literacy and strengthened their digital security capacity. The tailor-made support was designed for WHRDs by considering their gendered reality through increased digital literacy. WHRDs increased their awareness of threats online and on digital devices by incorporating gendered threats/risks. WHRDs strengthened their digital security through tools and skills they acquired in the trainings.
• 40 HRDs from conflict affected areas improved their understanding of physical and psychosocial security. They strengthened their understanding of physical risks/threats by conducting risk assessments. They have improved their skill to protect their psychological security through psychological first aid training.
Component 3: Strengthening human rights networking, advocacy, and communications capacity Results Achieved: • The activities here have resulted in participants having improved knowledge and skills in advocacy, communication, and branding. Also capacity support targeting at advocacy and joint actions have been provided, contributing to strengthen networking/solidarity.
• IPs, other human rights organisations and HRDs got the possibility of making a national assessment about the state of seven thematically grouped human rights in Ethiopia. The assessment and workshop held subsequently created an opportunity for HROs and HRDs to meet for the purpose of joint reflection and strategizing.
• The participation of HROs in the National Dialogue effort has been marginal and disorganised as it´s mostly dictated by other actors. The project enabled core HROs to produce the first structured and jointly developed National Dialogue Engagement Guideline for themselves. 21 organisations from 8 regional states took part in the consultation which was a learning and exchange opportunity. The Guideline outlines the principles of engaging HROs, they roles they can play, and which actors to target to be more effective.
• Implementing partners (HROs, HRDs and journalists) knowledge and skills in advocacy and universal human rights have been increased through the training workshops and grants. Partners have equipped themselves with the knowledge and data to promote themselves and human rights. For example, a partner in Benishangul Gumuz region assessed violations against minorities and engaged local authorities in a closed-door meeting to address the issue. Further, more than 100 women journalists got the opportunity to raise their knowledge about disabilities and disability-sensitive reporting. The platforms were also scenes of networking for journalists. And another partner monitored the state of democracy in 3 regional states (Sidama, Oromia and Gambella) and Addis Ababa, which in turn will be used for evidence-based advocacy. Ranking has been conducted to advocate for positive competition and change among regions.
• 12 HROs have been equipped with knowledge and skills that have improved their advocacy capacity. They have been able to develop advocacy strategies jointly and maximized their knowledge of human rights communication. The project has laid the path for coordinated advocacy through shared resources.
Source: CRD´s Annual Report Jan 2022-March 2023 (UM2020/15389/ADDI-48)
